lyrics:
[Intro: soft acoustic guitar, piano]

[Verse 1: plain, gentle male voice]
My old man could fix a tractor with a butter knife and wire
Could read the sky for rain, could coax a stubborn fire
But he never said the words, not once that I recall
His daddy never said 'em either. That's just how it was. That's all.

[Chorus: fuller, strings, sincere]
I never was a talker, I got that from you
We say it with a jump-start, a full tank, a fixed roof
But I don't want to leave it to a truck bed and a nod
I love you, Dad. I said it. That wasn't so hard.

[Verse 2: voice close, guitar and piano]
He looked down at the two-by-fours like they might have the reply
Cleared his throat and scratched his neck and wiped at one eye
Said, "These ain't gonna load themselves," and picked up his end
Then real quiet, by the tailgate: "Well. Me too, son."

[Chorus: fuller, strings, sincere]
I never was a talker, I got that from you
We say it with a jump-start, a full tank, a fixed roof
But I don't want to leave it to a truck bed and a nod
I love you, Dad. I said it. That wasn't so hard.

[Bridge: piano and voice]
My boy is six and says it twenty times a day
I say it back, every one
I'm not waiting till I'm gray

[Final Chorus: full band, warm]
I never was a talker, but I'm learning how to be
There's a little fella teaching what my daddy couldn't teach
And I won't leave it to a truck bed and a nod
I love you. There. I said it. That wasn't so hard.

[Outro: guitar, a tailgate closing]
